extractionNotes: COMPLETE extraction (Phase 9), done in a single session by reading the entire 199-page source PDF sequentially via pdftotext -layout (pdfPageIndex 1-199, in ~15 chunks). This subject branches into 3 mutually exclusive named specialisation options in Years 2-3: 'Option One — Automobile and Metal Technology' (Strands: Automotive Technology, Metal Technology), 'Option Two — Building Construction and Wood Technology' (Strands: Building Construction Technology, Wood Technology), 'Option Three — Electrical and Electronic Technology' (Strand: Electrical and Electronic Technology only). Year One is common to all learners (5 Strands, pathway=null). Each Year 2/3 Strand carries the exact printed option name in its 'pathway' field per the schema's 'Revisions after full inventory' guidance. Strand names are reused across years/options as separate Strand objects with distinct classLevel/pathway (15 Strand objects total: 5 Year-One shared + 5 Year-Two option strands + 5 Year-Three option strands), matching the convention established in physics.json (which repeats Strand names across SHS1/2/3 as separate objects) rather than nesting years under one Strand object.

FINAL TOTALS: 33 Content Standards / 32 Learning Outcomes / 176 Learning Indicators across the whole document. Breakdown: Year One (shared, SHS1) = 11 CS / 11 LO / 32 LI — EXACTLY matches the document's own Scope-and-Sequence 'Overall Totals (SHS 1)' table (pdfPageIndex 24). Option One (SHS2+SHS3 combined) = 8 CS / 8 LO / 48 LI — EXACTLY matches the document's own 'Overall Totals (SHS 2-3)' table for Option One (pdfPageIndex 25). Option Three (SHS2+SHS3 combined) = 4 CS / 4 LO / 48 LI — EXACTLY matches the document's own Option Three totals table (pdfPageIndex 26) exactly, including the unusually high 12-Learning-Indicators-per-Content-Standard pattern printed for both its sub-strands in both years. Option Two (SHS2+SHS3 combined, i.e. excluding Year One's Pre-Construction Activities sub-strand which the printed Option Two table folds in under a 'SHS 1-3' heading) = 10 CS / 9 LO / 48 LI in this file, vs the document's own printed 'Overall Totals (SHS 1-3)' table for Option Two of 10 CS / 9 LO / 49 LI (pdfPageIndex 25) — when Year One's Pre-Construction Activities (2 CS / 2 LO / 7 LI, part of the shared Building Construction Technology strand) is added to reproduce the table's own 'SHS 1-3' scope exactly as printed, this file's grand total for the full Option Two lineage is 12 CS / 11 LO / 55 LI, which does NOT exactly match the table's printed 10/9/49 — a real, not-reconciled discrepancy, most likely explained by the several genuine LO/CS code collisions documented below (the source prints two distinct Learning Outcomes/Content Standards under one shared code in three separate places in this Option), which this file counts as distinct objects (their content is genuinely different) rather than merging them down to match the table's collapsed count. Flagged, not silently reconciled.

Curriculum code formatting: the in-body Learning Outcome code for 1.1.1.LO.1 is printed with a formatting slip as '1.1.1L.O.1' (period misplaced inside 'LO') — this is the ONLY occurrence of this exact slip found across the whole document; all other Year One Learning Outcome codes use the standard '{Year}.{Strand}.{SubStrand}.LO.{Seq}' pattern. Preserved verbatim, flagged NEEDS_REVIEW.

Year One Sub-Strand 1.4.1 (Metal Technology > Engineering Materials, Tools and Machines): the third Learning Indicator under Content Standard 1.4.1.CS.1 is printed with the wrong sub-strand prefix '1.4.2.LI.3' (should be '1.4.1.LI.3' — it is physically located under Sub-Strand 1's Content Standard, not Sub-Strand 2's), and its paired Assessment code is likewise printed as '1.4.2.AS.3'. Preserved verbatim, flagged NEEDS_REVIEW.

Year One Sub-Strand 1.5.2 (Woodwork Technology > Materials and Artefacts Production): within Content Standard 1.5.2.CS.1's first Learning Indicator block, the second Assessment code is printed with the wrong year prefix '2.5.2.AS.2' (should be '1.5.2.AS.2') even though this is unambiguously Year One content. Preserved verbatim, flagged NEEDS_REVIEW.

Teaching and Learning Resources are printed once at the END of each Sub-Strand block (after all of its Content Standards), matching the canonical schema's illustrative example — unlike Physics/Robotics, no per-Content-Standard TLR splitting was needed for this subject (one exception: Year Three Electrical Systems Design's TLR block could not be located at all within its read page range — flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on that sub-strand rather than fabricated).

Three genuine Learning-Outcome/Content-Standard CODE COLLISIONS were found (two distinct LO/CS objects sharing one identical printed code, covering topically different content) — all preserved as separate objects with the collision documented via reviewNote/extractionNote rather than merged or renumbered: (1) Year Two Building Construction Technology Sub-Strand 'Substructure and Superstructure', both LOs printed as '2.3.2.LO.1'; (2) Year Three Wood Technology Sub-Strand 'Materials and Artefacts Production', both LOs AND both their aligned Content Standards printed as '3.4.2.LO.1'/'3.4.2.CS.1'.

The most severe anomaly in the whole document is in Year Three's Electrical and Electronic Technology Strand (Option Three): its own Strand heading number is inconsistent across years (Strand 3 in Year One, Strand 5 in Year Two, Strand 4 in Year Three), and critically, EVERY curriculum code printed within this Year Three Strand carries a wrong-Year prefix -- Sub-Strand 1 (Electrical Systems Design) uses '2.4.1.*' throughout (LO/CS/LI/AS), and Sub-Strand 2 (Electronic Components and Circuits) uses '2.4.2.LO.*' for its Learning Outcome but '2.5.2.*' for its Content Standard/Learning Indicators/Assessments -- none use the expected Year Three '3.*' prefix, and even the Strand-number component is internally inconsistent (4 vs 5) within this one Sub-Strand pairing. All 24 of this Strand's Learning Indicators are flagged NEEDS_REVIEW as a result. Despite the code chaos, the LEARNING-INDICATOR COUNT for both sub-strands (12 each) matches the document's own Scope-and-Sequence table exactly.

Widespread wrong-sub-strand-prefix pattern also found in Year Three Wood Technology Sub-Strand 'Materials and Artefacts Production': all 6 Assessment codes under its first Content Standard are printed as '3.6.2.AS.n' (there is no Strand 6 anywhere in this document) instead of the expected '3.4.2.AS.n'.

A recurring page-break/column-linearization rendering artifact (also seen in physics.json and other subjects in this corpus) scrambles the printed order of a small number of Learning Indicator/Assessment code labels relative to their description text across a page break, in about half a dozen places across this document (e.g. Year Two Automotive 2.1.2.LI.5/6, Year Two Metal 2.2.2.LI.3/4, Year Two Building Construction 2.3.2.CS.1's LI.4/5 Assessment pairing, Year Three Metal 3.2.2.LI.5/6). Content was reconstructed by matching description text to the DoK-level sequence in each case; the substance is preserved verbatim, only the pairing/ordering was inferred where the raw text order was ambiguous. Flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on each affected node.

Several Learning Indicators near the end of Sub-Strand blocks (typically the last LI before a page/section boundary) have no locatable printed Assessment code within the read page range -- these are stored with assessment.code: null and empty dokDescriptions/dokLevels rather than fabricated (Year Two Wood Technology 2.4.1.LI.4 and 2.4.2.LI.4/2.4.2.CS.2's LI.4; Year Three Electrical Systems Design LI.12; Year Three Electronic Components and Circuits LI.12).

86 nodes (Strand/Sub-Strand/Learning-Outcome/Content-Standard/Learning-Indicator level combined) are flagged NEEDS_REVIEW across the file, concentrated heavily in the Year Three Electrical and Electronic Technology Strand (24 LI + 2 CS + 2 LO = 28 nodes alone) due to its systematic wrong-prefix coding; the remainder are the individual collisions, missing TLR/Assessment blocks, and copy-paste-boilerplate cases itemised in this array and in each affected node's own reviewNote.

Checkpoint 6 Phase 1 correction (2026-09-29): Sub-Strand 1.5.2 (Woodwork Technology, SHS1) was originally extracted as a genuine shared-Content-Standard case (both 1.5.2.CS.1 and 1.5.2.CS.2 nested under 1.5.2.LO.1, with LO.2 left empty and a note that both Content Standards applied to both Learning Outcomes). Re-verified directly against curriculum-sources/Applied-Technology-Curriculum.pdf pages 61-64 (pdfPageIndex 63-66): each Content Standard's own wording and Learning Indicators separately and distinctly match one specific Learning Outcome, not both (1.5.2.CS.1 on timber classification matches LO.1; 1.5.2.CS.2 on manufactured boards is a near-verbatim match to LO.2's own description). Moved 1.5.2.CS.2 to 1.5.2.LO.2 and flagged both nodes NEEDS_REVIEW. This was the only Content-Standard/Learning-Outcome ambiguity in this file with clear-enough evidence for a Phase 1 correction; the Wood Technology (SHS2) Sub-Strand 'Materials and Artefact Production in Woodwork Industry in Ghana' genuinely has only 1 Learning Outcome with 2 Content Standards and no sibling to redistribute to - left blocked as a genuine multiple-Content-Standards case for the junction-table stage, not forced.

learningOutcomes.description: Analyse and use relevant principles underlying engines to service, and repair spark ignition (SI) and compression ignition (CI) engines

guidance.twentyFirstCenturySkills: Communication and collaboration skills: As learners work in groups they listen to peers and ask relevant questions based on what they heard, learning from and contributing to the learning of others, and adapt their presentation to better engage the audience. Able to identify and analyse different points of view they hear in a discussion and explain how they are different. Critical thinking and Problem-solving skills: Ability to use justifiable principles to choose between the types that they have identified; apply knowledge to real life workings in the use of engines; apply their knowledge or make connections with what they learn in real life situations.
guidance.gesi: Learners having experienced a teaching approach that ensures gender equality and social inclusion, where they work with each other in an inclusive way; cross-sharing knowledge and understanding among groups and individuals lead them to: examine and dispel misconceptions/myths about gender as they relate to technical education; interrogate their stereotypes and biases about gender and the role men and women play in technical education; be sensitive to the interrelatedness of the various aspects of engine systems; value and promote health and safety in workshop and in society.
guidance.sel: All learning experiences related to engine technology should give learners the opportunities to develop the social emotional learning competencies, which include self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, and responsible decision-making. The teacher should implement the social emotional learning strategies to make sure that learners achieve each learning outcome in the engine technology and be: reflecting about oneself and gaining confidence; exhibiting motivation and SMART goal setting; managing feelings, emotions and conflicts; showing empathy and cooperation. Strategies: modelling emotional self-control and judgment; promotion of positive self-talk with self-made portraits of engineering practices; making of a vision board, coming up with respectful conversation starters for healthy debates; encourage learners to write about the sequence of their activities and diversity presentations.

subStrands.name: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS DESIGN
teachingLearningResources: computers installed with VPLab, multism and circuit wizard software

learningOutcomes.description: Outline clearly, safety principles to follow in the use of electricity; analyse the key steps in power transmission and link it to power distribution to other substations, homes and industries.

guidance.twentyFirstCenturySkills: Communication Skills: Learners work in groups thus enabling them to become capable of listening and participating in a group discussion, as well as being able to express themselves well when the need arises. Collaboration Skills: Learners appreciate the views of others. Critical Thinking skills: the use of brainstorming enables learners to develop the ability to think critically and seek additional information. Problem Solving Skills: learners develop the ability to think rationally when confronted with a situation. Digital Literacy: learners can do presentations using power point and use ICT to access Open Educational Resources on the internet (OERs). Personal development, Leadership, and Creativity and Innovation skills are also developed through working with others and interpreting ideas.
guidance.gesi: The classroom is always made up of learners of various backgrounds with unique needs and challenges. It is therefore very important to ensure that all teaching and learning approaches promote gender equality and social inclusion. Learners who experience such approaches are more likely to: value and respect individuals of different backgrounds in order to understand them when they make different choices during analysis of electrical issues; be gender sensitive and so value and appreciate the diverse roles played by men, women and persons with special needs during electrical works that demand physical activities e.g. poles/pylons climbing as well as dismantling of electrical machines; appreciate diversity and practice inclusion by involving all in electrical works.
guidance.sel: The instructional methods used to ensure social inclusion, social justice, and emotional control have been introduced to the students. Learning through SEL allows students to make decisions and adhere to safety precautions when working with electricity; be aware of his/her strength and weaknesses as far as the learning of power transmission and distribution is concerned; be able to relate to other learners when group assignments are given; be able to manage his/her time very well when given individual assignment.
